units.Wisdom of Solomon 9:1: “God of the fathers and Lord of mercy, who made all things by Thy word

units.Job 9:4: For He is wise in understanding, mighty and great. Who grew hard against Him and endured?

units.Job 9:6: He shakes the world beneath heaven from its foundations, and its pillars sway.
units.Job 9:7: He speaks to the sun and it does not rise, and He seals up the stars.

units.Job 9:10: He does great and unsearchable things, glorious and extraordinary things beyond numbering.

units.Psalms 144:1: A praise of David. I will exalt Thee, my God, my King, and bless Thy name for the age and for the age of the age.
units.Psalms 144:2: Every day I will bless Thee and praise Thy name for the age and for the age of the age.
units.Psalms 144:3: Great is the Lord and greatly to be praised; His greatness has no limit.
units.Psalms 144:4: Generation after generation will praise Thy works, and they will declare Thy power.
units.Psalms 144:5: They will speak of the magnificence of the glory of Thy holiness, and they will recount Thy wonders.
units.Psalms 144:6: They will speak of the power of Thy fearsome acts, and they will recount Thy greatness.
units.Psalms 144:7: They will pour forth remembrance of the abundance of Thy kindness and rejoice in Thy righteousness.
units.Psalms 144:8: Compassionate and merciful is the Lord, patient and abundant in mercy.
units.Psalms 144:9: The Lord is kind to all, and His compassions are over all His works.
units.Psalms 144:10: Let all Thy works give thanks unto Thee, Lord, and let Thy holy ones bless Thee.
units.Psalms 144:11: They will speak of the glory of Thy kingdom and tell of Thy might,
units.Psalms 144:12: to make known to the sons of men Thy might and the glory of the magnificence of Thy kingdom.
units.Psalms 144:13: Thy kingdom is a kingdom of all ages, and Thy lordship endures through every generation.
units.Ecclesiastes 3:10: I saw the distraction God has given human beings to be distracted by.
units.Ecclesiastes 3:11: He has made everything beautiful in its time. He has also put the age in their hearts, so that human beings may not find out the work God has done from beginning to end.
units.Ecclesiastes 3:12: I knew that there is no good for them except to rejoice and do good during one’s life.

units.Ecclesiastes 3:15: What has come to be already is, and whatever is to come has already come to be; God will seek the one who is pursued.

units.Psalms 89:1: A prayer of Moses, the man of God. Lord, Thou becamest our refuge through every generation.
units.Psalms 89:2: Before the mountains came to be and the earth and inhabited world were formed, from age to age Thou art.
units.Psalms 89:3: Do not turn a man toward humiliation; and Thou saidst, Return, sons of men.
units.Psalms 89:4: For a thousand years in Thine eyes are like yesterday, which passed, and a watch in the night.
units.Psalms 89:5: Their things counted as nothing will be years. In the morning, like green grass, may it pass away;
units.Psalms 89:6: in the morning may it blossom and pass away; in the evening may it fall, grow hard and dry up.
units.Psalms 89:7: For we failed in Thine anger and were troubled in Thy wrath.
units.Psalms 89:8: Thou didst set our lawless deeds before Thee; our age is in the light of Thy face.
units.Psalms 89:9: For all our days failed, and in Thine anger we failed; I pondered our years like a spider.
units.Psalms 89:10: The days of our years—in them are seventy years, or, with strength, eighty years; the greater part of them is toil and pain, for gentleness came upon us, and we shall be disciplined.
units.Psalms 89:11: Who knows the might of Thine anger, and Thy wrath from the fear of Thee?
units.Psalms 89:12: So make known how to number Thy right hand, and those bound in heart in wisdom.
units.Psalms 102:8: The Lord is compassionate and merciful, patient and abundant in mercy.
units.Psalms 102:9: He will not be angry to the end, nor maintain wrath for ever.
units.Psalms 102:10: He has not dealt with us according to our sins, nor repaid us according to our lawless deeds,
units.Psalms 102:11: for according to heaven’s height above the earth, the Lord strengthened His mercy toward those who fear Him.
units.Psalms 102:12: As far as the east is distant from the west, He removed our lawless deeds from us.
units.Psalms 102:13: As a father has compassion on children, the Lord had compassion on those who fear Him,
units.Psalms 102:14: for He knew our formation. Remember that we are dust.
units.Psalms 102:15: A man—his days are like grass; like a flower of the field, so he will flower,
units.Psalms 102:16: for a wind passed through him, and he will not exist, and he will no longer recognize his place.
units.Psalms 102:17: But the Lord’s mercy is from eternity to eternity toward those who fear Him, and His righteousness toward children’s children,
units.Psalms 102:18: to those who keep His covenant and remember His commandments to do them.

units.Proverbs 3:11: Son, do not make light of the Lord’s discipline or lose heart when corrected by Him,

units.Proverbs 3:13: Blessed is the person who found wisdom, the mortal who saw good sense,
units.Proverbs 3:14: for trading in her is better than treasures of gold and silver.
units.Proverbs 3:15: She is more valuable than costly stones; nothing evil will stand against her. She is readily known to all who approach her, and nothing precious is worthy of her.
units.Proverbs 3:16: For length of life and years of living are in her right hand, and wealth and glory in her left.
units.Proverbs 3:16a: Righteousness proceeds from her mouth, and she carries law and mercy on her tongue.
units.Proverbs 3:17: Her ways are good ways, and all her paths are in peace.
units.Proverbs 3:18: She is a tree of life to all who hold her fast, and secure for those who lean on her as on the Lord.
units.James 1:2: Count it all joy, my brothers, whenever you encounter trials of various kinds,
units.James 1:3: knowing that the testing of your faith produces endurance.
units.James 1:4: And let endurance have its complete work, so that you may be complete and whole, lacking in nothing.
units.James 1:5: But if any of you lacks wisdom, let him ask God, who gives to all generously and without reproach, and it will be given to him.
units.James 1:6: But let him ask in faith, doubting nothing, for the one who doubts is like a wave of the sea, driven and tossed by the wind.
units.James 1:7: For that person must not suppose that he will receive anything from the Lord,
units.James 1:8: a man of divided mind, unstable in all his ways.
units.Proverbs 15:20: A wise son makes a father glad, but a foolish son sneers at his mother.
units.Proverbs 15:21: The paths of a senseless person lack understanding, but an intelligent man walks making his course straight.
units.Proverbs 15:22: Those who do not honor councils put plans off, but counsel remains in the hearts of those who deliberate.
units.Proverbs 15:23: The evil person will certainly not heed it, nor say anything timely and good for the community.

units.Proverbs 15:26: An unjust thought is an abomination to the Lord, but the sayings of pure people are noble.
units.Proverbs 15:27: One who takes bribes destroys himself, but one who hates taking gifts is saved.

units.Proverbs 15:29: God is far distant from the impious, but He listens to the prayers of the righteous.

units.Ecclesiastes 5:1: Do not be hasty with your mouth, and do not let your heart hurry to bring out a word before God, for God is in heaven and you are on earth. Therefore let your words be few.
units.Ecclesiastes 5:2: For a dream comes with much distraction, and a fool’s voice with many words.
units.Ecclesiastes 5:3: Whenever you vow a vow to God, do not delay paying it, for there is no delight in fools. Pay whatever you vow.
units.Ecclesiastes 5:4: Better that you do not vow than that you vow and do not pay.
units.Ecclesiastes 5:5: Do not let your mouth cause your flesh to sin, and do not say before God, “It was ignorance,” lest God become angry at your voice and destroy the works of your hands.
units.Ecclesiastes 5:6: For with many dreams come futilities and many words; therefore fear God.

units.Galatians 5:16: But I say, walk by the Spirit, and you will certainly not fulfill the desire of the flesh.
units.Galatians 5:17: For the flesh desires what is against the Spirit, and the Spirit what is against the flesh; for these oppose one another, so that you do not do the things you want.
units.Galatians 5:18: But if you are led by the Spirit, you are not under law.
units.Galatians 5:19: Now the works of the flesh are evident: sexual immorality, impurity, licentiousness,
units.Galatians 5:20: idolatry, sorcery, hostilities, strife, jealousy, outbursts of anger, selfish ambitions, divisions, factions,
units.Galatians 5:21: envies, drunkenness, revelries, and things like these. I tell you beforehand, just as I told you before, that those who practice such things will not inherit the kingdom of God.
units.Galatians 5:22: But the fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, patience, kindness, goodness, faithfulness,

units.James 3:1: Not many of you should become teachers, my brothers, knowing that we will receive a greater judgment.

units.Psalms 77:1: Of understanding. Of Asaph. Attend, my people, to my law; bend your ear to the words of my mouth.
units.Psalms 77:2: I will open my mouth in parables; I will utter riddles from the beginning,
units.Psalms 77:3: whatever we heard and knew, and our fathers recounted to us,
units.Psalms 77:4: it was not hidden from their children for another generation, as we announce the Lord’s praises, His mighty acts and the wonders He did.
units.Psalms 77:5: And He raised a testimony in Jacob and set a law in Israel, whatever He commanded our fathers to make known to their sons,
units.Psalms 77:6: so that another generation might know, sons who will be born; and they will rise and announce it to their sons,
units.Psalms 77:7: so that they may set their hope upon God and not forget God’s works, and seek out His commandments,
units.Psalms 77:8: so that they may not become like their fathers, a crooked and embittering generation, a generation that did not direct its heart, whose spirit was not faithful with God.
units.Sirach 33:16: I too, the last, kept watch like someone gleaning behind grape-gatherers.
units.Sirach 33:17: By the Lord’s blessing I came in time, and like a grape-gatherer I filled a winepress.
units.Sirach 33:18: Consider that I have labored not for myself alone, but for all who seek instruction.
units.Sirach 33:19: Listen to me, dignitaries of the people; give ear, leaders of the assembly.
units.Psalms 132:1: A song of the ascents. For David. Behold, what is good or what is delightful except for brothers to dwell together?
units.Psalms 132:2: Like ointment upon the head, descending upon the beard, Aaron’s beard, descending upon the border of his garment;
units.Psalms 132:3: Like Hermon’s dew descending upon Zion’s mountains; for there the Lord commanded the blessing and life for ever.
units.Job 12:11: For the ear discerns words, and the throat tastes food.
units.Job 12:12: In much time is wisdom, and in a long life knowledge.
units.Job 12:13: With Him are wisdom and power; to Him belong counsel and understanding.
units.Job 32:6: Elihu son of Barachel the Buzite replied: “I am younger in time, and you are older; therefore I kept quiet, afraid to announce my own knowledge to you.
units.Job 32:7: I said, ‘Time is what speaks, and in many years people know wisdom.’
units.Job 32:8: But there is a spirit in mortals, and the Almighty’s breath is what teaches.
units.Job 32:9: The long-lived are not wise, nor do elders know judgment.
units.Job 32:10: Therefore I said, ‘Listen to me, and I will announce to you what I know.’
units.Proverbs 16:31: Old age is a crown of boasting, and it is found in ways of righteousness.
units.Proverbs 16:32: A patient man is better than a strong man, and one who controls anger is better than one who captures a city.
units.Proverbs 16:33: Everything comes into the laps of the unjust, but all righteous things are from the Lord.
units.Proverbs 23:24: A righteous father brings up well, and his life rejoices over a wise son;
units.Proverbs 23:25: let father and mother rejoice over you, and let the one who bore you be glad.
units.Proverbs 23:26: Give me your heart, son, and let your eyes keep my ways;
units.Proverbs 23:27: for another’s house is a jar with holes, and another’s well is narrow;
units.Proverbs 23:28: for this will swiftly perish, and every lawless person will be consumed.
units.Proverbs 19:13: A foolish son is shame to a father, and prayers from a courtesan’s fee are not pure.
units.Proverbs 19:14: Fathers apportion house and property to children, but a wife is joined to a husband by God.
units.Proverbs 21:17: A needy man loves gladness, loving wine and oil toward wealth;
units.Proverbs 21:18: but a lawless person is a cleansing-offering for the righteous.
units.Proverbs 21:19: Better to dwell in a desert land than with a battling, talkative, and quick-tempered woman.
units.Proverbs 27:15: Drops drive a man from his house on a wintry day, and likewise an abusive wife from his own house.
units.Proverbs 27:16: The north wind is a harsh wind, but by name it is called favorable.
units.Genesis 3:6: And the woman saw that the tree was good for food, pleasing to the eyes, and beautiful to contemplate. And she took of its fruit and ate; she also gave some to her husband with her, and they ate.
units.Genesis 3:7: And the eyes of both were opened, and they knew that they were naked. And they sewed fig leaves together and made coverings for themselves.
units.Genesis 3:8: And they heard the sound of the Lord God walking in the garden toward evening. And Adam and his wife hid themselves from the face of the Lord God among the trees of the garden.
units.Genesis 3:9: And the Lord God called to Adam and said to him, “Adam, where are you?”
units.Genesis 3:10: And he said to Him, “I heard Thy voice as Thou didst walk in the garden, and I was afraid because I am naked, and I hid myself.”
units.Genesis 3:11: And He said to him, “Who told you that you are naked? Have you eaten from the tree of which alone I commanded you not to eat?”
units.Genesis 3:12: And Adam said, “The woman whom Thou didst give to be with me—she gave me fruit from the tree, and I ate.”
units.Genesis 3:13: And the Lord God said to the woman, “What is this you have done?” And the woman said, “The serpent deceived me, and I ate.”
units.Genesis 3:14: And the Lord God said to the serpent: Because you have done this, cursed are you above all cattle and all the wild beasts of the earth. Upon your breast and belly you shall go, and earth you shall eat all the days of your life.
units.Genesis 3:15: And I will put enmity between you and the woman, and between your seed and her seed. He shall watch for your head, and you shall watch for his heel.
units.Genesis 3:16: And to the woman He said: I will greatly multiply your sorrows and your groaning; in sorrow you shall bear children. You shall turn toward your husband, and he shall rule over you.
units.Genesis 3:17: And to Adam He said: Because you listened to the voice of your wife and ate from the tree of which alone I commanded you not to eat, cursed is the earth in your labours; in pain you shall eat of it all the days of your life.
units.Genesis 3:18: Thorns and thistles it shall bring forth for you, and you shall eat the plants of the field.
units.Genesis 3:19: By the sweat of your face you shall eat your bread, until you return to the earth from which you were taken; for earth you are, and unto earth you shall return.
units.Proverbs 17:12: Concern will fall upon an intelligent man, but fools will deliberate evil things.
units.Proverbs 17:13: One who repays evil things instead of good things—evils will not move from his house.
units.Proverbs 17:14: The beginning of righteousness gives authority to words, but faction and battle lead the way to want.
units.Proverbs 17:15: One who judges the unjust righteous and the righteous unjust is unclean and detestable before God.
units.Genesis 2:18: And the Lord God said, “It is not good for the man to be alone. Let Us make him a helper corresponding to him.”
units.Genesis 2:19: And God also formed from the earth every wild beast of the field and every bird of heaven, and brought them to Adam to see what he would call them. And whatever Adam called each living creature, that was its name.
units.Genesis 2:20: And Adam gave names to all the cattle, all the birds of heaven, and all the wild beasts of the field. But for Adam no helper like himself was found.
units.Genesis 2:21: And God cast a deep sleep upon Adam, and he slept. And He took one of his ribs and filled its place with flesh.
units.Genesis 2:22: And the Lord God fashioned the rib He had taken from Adam into a woman, and brought her to Adam.
units.Genesis 2:23: And Adam said: This, at last, is bone of my bones and flesh of my flesh. She shall be called Woman, for she was taken from her husband.
units.Genesis 2:24: For this reason a man shall leave his father and his mother and cleave to his wife, and the two shall become one flesh.
units.Genesis 2:25: And the two were naked, both Adam and his wife, and they were not ashamed.
units.Deuteronomy 24:1: And if a man takes a wife and dwells with her as husband, and she finds no favour in his sight, because he has found some unseemly thing in her, and he writes her a certificate of divorce, and gives it into her hands, and sends her forth out of his house,
units.Deuteronomy 24:2: and she departs and becomes another man’s wife,
units.Deuteronomy 24:3: and the latter husband hates her, and writes her a certificate of divorce, and gives it into her hands, and sends her forth out of his house, or if the latter husband who took her to be his wife dies,
units.Deuteronomy 24:4: her former husband, who sent her away, may not take her again to be his wife, after she has been defiled; for it is an abomination before the Lord your God. And you shall not defile the land which the Lord your God gives you for a possession.
units.Wisdom of Solomon 7:22: For in her is a spirit intelligent, holy, unique, manifold, subtle, agile, lucid, undefiled, clear, unharmed, loving the good, keen,
units.Wisdom of Solomon 7:23: unhindered, beneficent, loving humanity, steadfast, secure, free from care, all-powerful, all-overseeing, and passing through all spirits that are intelligent, pure, and most subtle.
units.Wisdom of Solomon 7:24: For wisdom is more mobile than every motion; she penetrates and passes through all things because of her purity.
units.Wisdom of Solomon 7:25: For she is a breath of God’s power and a pure outflow of the Almighty’s glory; therefore nothing defiled enters into her.
units.Wisdom of Solomon 7:26: For she is a radiance of eternal light, an unstained mirror of God’s activity, and an image of His goodness.
units.Sirach 26:1: Happy is the husband of a good wife, and the number of his days is doubled.
units.Sirach 26:2: A courageous wife gladdens her husband, and he will complete his years in peace.
units.Sirach 26:3: A good wife is a good portion; she will be given among the portion of those who fear the Lord.
units.Sirach 26:4: Whether rich or poor, his heart is good, and at every time his face is cheerful.
units.Sirach 18:1: He who lives for ever created all things together.
units.Sirach 18:2: The Lord alone will be justified.
units.Sirach 18:4: He has empowered no one to declare His works fully; who will trace out His mighty deeds?
units.Sirach 18:5: Who will count the might of His greatness? Who will go on to recount His mercies?
units.Sirach 18:6: It is impossible to diminish or to add, and impossible to trace out the Lord’s wonders.
units.Sirach 18:7: When a person finishes, then he begins; when he stops, then he will be at a loss.
units.Sirach 18:8: What is a human being, and what is his use? What is his good, and what is his evil?
units.Sirach 18:9: The number of a person’s days, in many years, is a hundred.
units.Sirach 18:10: Like a drop of water from the sea or a grain of sand, so are a few years in a day of eternity.
units.Sirach 18:11: Therefore the Lord was patient with them and poured His mercy upon them.
units.Sirach 18:12: He saw and knew that their end was grievous; therefore He multiplied His atonement.
units.Sirach 18:13: A person’s mercy is toward his neighbor, but the Lord’s mercy is upon all flesh: rebuking, disciplining, teaching, and bringing back like a shepherd his flock.
units.Sirach 18:14: He has mercy on those who receive discipline and those who hasten eagerly toward His judgments.
units.Sirach 18:15: Child, do not add reproach to good deeds, or the grief of words to any gift.
units.Sirach 18:16: Will not dew bring relief from scorching heat? So a word is better than a gift.
units.Sirach 18:17: Behold, is not a word beyond a good gift? Yet both are found with a gracious man.
units.Sirach 18:18: A fool will reproach gracelessly, and a grudging person’s gift makes eyes waste away.
units.Sirach 18:19: Learn before speaking, and attend to your health before illness.
units.Sirach 18:20: Examine yourself before judgment, and at the hour of visitation you will find atonement.
units.Sirach 18:21: Humble yourself before you fall ill, and show repentance at the time of sins.
units.Sirach 18:22: Do not be held back from repaying a vow at the right time, and do not wait until death to be justified.
units.Sirach 18:23: Prepare yourself before making a vow, and do not become like a person testing the Lord.
units.Sirach 18:24: Remember wrath in the days of death, and the time of retribution when the face is turned away.
units.Sirach 18:25: Remember a time of famine in a time of fullness, poverty and need in days of wealth.
units.Sirach 18:26: From morning until evening the time changes, and all things are swift before the Lord.
units.Sirach 18:27: A wise person will be cautious in everything, and in days of sins will guard against wrongdoing.
units.Sirach 18:28: Every understanding person has known wisdom and will give acknowledgment to the one who finds her.
units.Sirach 18:29: Those understanding in words have themselves become wise and rained down precise proverbs.
units.Sirach 18:30: Do not walk after your desires, and restrain your appetites.
units.Sirach 18:31: If you supply your soul with the satisfaction of desire, it will make you an object of your enemies’ gloating.
units.Sirach 18:32: Do not rejoice in great luxury, lest you be bound to contribute to it.
units.Sirach 18:33: Do not become poor by feasting on borrowed money when you have nothing in your purse.
units.Sirach 19:1: A drunken worker will not become rich; the one who despises small things will fall little by little.
units.Sirach 19:2: Wine and women will lead understanding men astray, and the one who clings to prostitutes will become more reckless.
units.Sirach 19:3: Rot and worms will inherit him, and a reckless soul will be taken away.
units.Sirach 19:4: The one who trusts quickly is lighthearted, and the one who sins will wrong his own soul.
units.Sirach 19:5: The one who rejoices in heart will be condemned,
units.Sirach 19:6: but the one who hates chatter diminishes evil.
units.Sirach 19:7: Never repeat a word, and you will certainly lose nothing.
units.Sirach 19:8: Do not tell it to friend or enemy, and unless silence is a sin for you, do not reveal it.
units.Sirach 19:9: For someone has heard you and kept watch on you, and in time he will hate you.
units.Sirach 19:10: Have you heard a word? Let it die with you. Take courage; it will certainly not make you burst.
units.Sirach 19:11: A fool will suffer labor pains over a word, like a woman giving birth over her baby.
units.Sirach 19:12: An arrow fixed in the flesh of a thigh—so is a word in a fool’s belly.
units.Sirach 19:13: Question a friend; perhaps he did not do it, and if he did, question him so that he may not repeat it.
units.Sirach 19:14: Question your neighbor; perhaps he did not say it, and if he has said it, question him so that he may not say it again.
units.Sirach 19:15: Question a friend, for slander often occurs; do not trust every report.
units.Sirach 19:16: There is someone who slips without intending it in his soul; who has not sinned with his tongue?
units.Sirach 19:17: Question your neighbor before threatening him, and give place to the law of the Most High.
units.Sirach 19:20: All wisdom is fear of the Lord, and in all wisdom there is doing the law.
units.Sirach 19:22: Knowledge of wickedness is not wisdom, and where sinners take counsel there is no prudence.
units.Sirach 19:23: There is shrewdness that is an abomination, and there is a foolish person deficient in wisdom.
units.Sirach 19:24: Better someone lacking understanding but full of fear than someone abounding in prudence who transgresses the law.
units.Sirach 19:25: There is precise shrewdness that is unjust, and there is someone who twists matters in order to bring a judgment to light.
units.Sirach 19:26: There is someone who acts wickedly while bowed down in gloom, with his inward parts full of deceit.
units.Sirach 19:27: Hiding his face and pretending to be deaf, where he has not been recognized he will get ahead of you.
units.Sirach 19:28: If lack of strength prevents him from sinning, he will do evil when he finds an opportunity.
units.Sirach 19:29: A man will be recognized from his appearance, and an understanding person from the look of his face.
units.Sirach 19:30: A man’s clothing, the grin of his teeth, and a person’s steps will declare what he is like.
units.Sirach 20:1: There is a rebuke that is not fitting, and there is a silent person who is prudent.
units.Sirach 20:2: How much better to rebuke than to be angry,
units.Sirach 20:3: and the one who acknowledges his fault will be kept from loss.
units.Sirach 20:4: A eunuch’s desire to take a young woman’s virginity—so is the one who carries out judgments by force.
units.Sirach 20:5: There is a silent person who is found wise, and there is someone hated for much chatter.
units.Sirach 20:6: There is someone silent because he has no answer, and someone silent because he knows the right time.
units.Sirach 20:7: A wise person will keep silent until the right time, but a babbler and a fool will miss the right time.
units.Sirach 20:8: The one who multiplies words will be loathed, and the one who assumes authority will be hated.
units.Sirach 20:9: There is success for a man amid adversity, and there is a gain that brings loss.
units.Sirach 20:10: There is a gift that will not benefit you, and a gift whose repayment is double.
units.Sirach 20:11: There is loss for the sake of glory, and there is someone who has lifted his head from lowliness.
units.Sirach 20:12: There is someone who buys much for little and pays for it sevenfold.
units.Sirach 20:13: A wise person will make himself welcome by his words, but fools’ favors will be wasted.
units.Sirach 20:14: An unthinking person’s gift will not benefit you, for his eyes seek many things in exchange for one.
units.Sirach 20:15: He will give little and reproach much, and open his mouth like a herald. Today he will lend, and tomorrow he will demand repayment; such a person is hateful.
units.Sirach 20:16: A fool will say, “I have no friend, and there is no gratitude for my good deeds.”
units.Sirach 20:17: Those who eat his bread are base in speech. How often, and how many, will laugh at him?
units.Sirach 20:18: Better a slip on the ground than a slip of the tongue; so the fall of the wicked will come swiftly.
units.Sirach 20:19: A graceless person is an untimely tale; it will be continually in the mouth of the uninstructed.
units.Sirach 20:20: A proverb will be rejected from a fool’s mouth, for he will certainly not say it at its proper time.
units.Sirach 20:21: There is someone prevented from sinning by need; in his rest he will not be pierced with remorse.
units.Sirach 20:22: There is someone who destroys his soul through shame, and through regard for a foolish face he will lose it.
units.Sirach 20:23: There is someone who makes a promise to a friend because of shame, and has acquired him as an enemy for nothing.
units.Sirach 20:24: A lie is an evil blemish in a person; it will be continually in the mouth of the uninstructed.
units.Sirach 20:25: A thief is preferable to someone who persists in lying, but both will inherit destruction.
units.Sirach 20:26: A lying person’s character is dishonor, and his shame is continually with him.
units.Sirach 20:27: A wise person will advance himself through his words, and a prudent man will please dignitaries.
units.Sirach 20:28: The one who works the land will raise his heap of grain, and the one who pleases dignitaries will atone for injustice.
units.Sirach 20:29: Presents and gifts blind the eyes of the wise and turn aside rebukes like a muzzle in the mouth.
units.Sirach 20:30: Hidden wisdom and an unseen treasure—what benefit is there in either?
units.Sirach 20:31: Better a person who hides his foolishness than a person who hides his wisdom.
units.Sirach 21:1: Child, have you sinned? Do not add to it any more, and pray concerning your earlier sins.
units.Sirach 21:2: Flee from sin as from the presence of a snake, for if you approach it, it will bite you. Its teeth are lions’ teeth, destroying human lives.
units.Sirach 21:3: All lawlessness is like a two-edged sword; there is no healing for its wound.
units.Sirach 21:4: Intimidation and insolence will lay wealth waste; so the house of a proud person will be laid waste.
units.Sirach 21:5: A poor person’s petition goes from his mouth to His ears, and His judgment comes swiftly.
units.Sirach 21:6: The one who hates rebuke is in a sinner’s tracks, but the one who fears the Lord will turn back in heart.
units.Sirach 21:7: One who is powerful with the tongue is known from far away, but an understanding person knows when he slips.
units.Sirach 21:8: The one who builds his house with others’ money is like someone gathering its stones for a storm.
units.Sirach 21:9: An assembly of the lawless is gathered tow, and their end is a flame of fire.
units.Sirach 21:10: The sinners’ road is smoothed with stones, but at its end is the pit of Hades.
units.Sirach 21:11: The one who keeps the law masters his thoughts, and wisdom is the fulfillment of the fear of the Lord.
units.Sirach 21:12: The one who is not shrewd will not be instructed, yet there is a shrewdness that multiplies bitterness.
units.Sirach 21:13: A wise person’s knowledge will increase like a flood, and his counsel is like a spring of life.
units.Sirach 21:14: A fool’s inward parts are like a broken vessel; he will retain no knowledge.
units.Sirach 21:15: If a knowledgeable person hears a wise word, he will praise it and add to it. A self-indulgent person heard it, and it displeased him; he cast it behind his back.
units.Sirach 21:16: A fool’s explanation is like a burden on a journey, but grace will be found on an understanding person’s lip.
units.Sirach 21:17: The mouth of a prudent person will be sought in the assembly, and they will consider his words in their heart.
units.Sirach 21:18: Wisdom is like a ruined house to a fool, and an uncomprehending person’s knowledge is unexamined words.
units.Sirach 21:19: Instruction is fetters on the feet of the senseless, and like handcuffs on his right hand.
units.Sirach 21:20: A fool raises his voice in laughter, but a shrewd man will barely smile quietly.
units.Sirach 21:21: Instruction is like a golden ornament to the prudent, and like a bracelet on his right arm.
units.Sirach 21:22: A fool’s foot is quick to enter a house, but an experienced person will feel shame before it.
units.Sirach 21:23: A foolish person peers into a house from its door, but an instructed man will stand outside.
units.Sirach 21:24: It is a person’s lack of instruction to listen at a door, but the prudent will feel weighed down by the dishonor.
units.Sirach 21:25: Strangers’ lips will talk about these things, but the words of the prudent will be weighed in a balance.
units.Sirach 21:26: Fools have their heart in their mouth, but the heart of the wise is their mouth.
units.Sirach 21:27: When an ungodly person curses Satan, he curses his own soul.
units.Sirach 21:28: The whisperer stains his own soul and will be hated where he dwells.
units.Sirach 22:1: A lazy person has been compared to a filthy stone, and everyone will hiss at his dishonor.
units.Sirach 22:2: A lazy person has been compared to a lump of dung; everyone who picks it up will shake his hand.
units.Sirach 22:3: A father’s shame is in begetting an uninstructed child, and a daughter brings about loss.
units.Sirach 22:4: A prudent daughter will inherit her husband, but one who brings shame brings grief to her parent.
units.Sirach 22:5: A shameless woman shames both father and husband and will be dishonored by both.
units.Sirach 22:6: An untimely discourse is music in mourning, but lashes and discipline are wisdom at every time.
units.Sirach 22:9: The one teaching a fool is gluing a potsherd together, waking a sleeper from deep sleep.
units.Sirach 22:10: The one speaking to a fool is speaking to someone drowsy; at the end he will say, “What is it?”
units.Sirach 22:11: Weep over a dead person, for he has lost the light; weep also over a fool, for he has lost understanding. Weep more gently over the dead, because he has found rest, but the fool’s life is worse than death.
units.Sirach 22:12: Mourning for the dead lasts seven days; for a fool and an ungodly person, all the days of his life.
units.Sirach 22:13: Do not multiply words with a fool or go to someone without understanding. Guard against him so that you do not have trouble, and you will certainly not be stained by what he shakes off. Turn away from him, and you will find rest and will certainly not grow weary of his madness.
units.Sirach 22:14: What is heavier than lead? What is its name except a fool?
units.Sirach 22:15: Sand, salt, and a lump of iron are easier to bear than a person without understanding.
units.Sirach 22:16: A wooden bond fitted into a building will not be loosened in a shaking; so a heart established on thoughtful counsel will not be cowardly when the time comes.
units.Sirach 22:17: A heart made firm upon an understanding thought is like a sanded ornament on a polished wall.
units.Sirach 22:18: Stakes set on a height will certainly not endure before the wind; so a cowardly heart resting on a foolish thought will certainly not endure before any fear.
units.Sirach 22:19: The one who pricks an eye will bring down tears; the one who pricks a heart reveals feeling.
units.Sirach 22:20: Throwing a stone at birds drives them away, and the one who reproaches a friend will break up friendship.
units.Sirach 22:21: If you draw a sword against a friend, do not despair, for there is a way back.
units.Sirach 22:22: If you open your mouth against a friend, do not be afraid, for there is reconciliation—except for reproach, pride, disclosure of a secret, and a treacherous blow; at these things every friend will flee.
units.Sirach 22:23: Establish trust with your neighbor in poverty, so that you may be filled together with him in his good circumstances. Stay with him in a time of affliction, so that you may share his inheritance.
units.Sirach 22:24: Before fire come a furnace’s vapor and smoke; so before bloodshed come insults.
units.Sirach 22:25: I will not be ashamed to shelter a friend, and I will certainly not hide from his face.
units.Sirach 22:26: If evil things happen to me because of him, everyone who hears will guard against him.
units.Sirach 22:27: Who will place a guard upon my mouth and a skillful seal upon my lips, so that I do not fall because of it and my tongue destroy me?
units.Sirach 23:1: Lord, Father and Master of my life, do not abandon me to their counsel; do not let me fall through them.
units.Sirach 23:2: Who will set lashes over my thought and wisdom’s discipline over my heart, so that they may not spare my errors of ignorance, and He may certainly not pass over their sins,
units.Sirach 23:3: so that my errors of ignorance do not multiply and my sins increase, and I fall before my adversaries and my enemy gloat over me?
units.Sirach 23:4: Lord, Father and God of my life, do not give me haughty eyes,
units.Sirach 23:5: and turn desire away from me.
units.Sirach 23:6: Do not let the appetite of the belly and sexual intercourse overtake me, and do not hand me over to a shameless soul.
units.Sirach 23:7: Listen, children, to discipline of the mouth; the one who keeps it will certainly not be caught.
units.Sirach 23:8: A sinner will be caught by his lips, and an abusive person and a proud person will stumble through them.
units.Sirach 23:9: Do not accustom your mouth to an oath, and do not make a habit of naming the Holy One.
units.Sirach 23:10: For just as a household slave under continual examination will not be free of bruises, so the one who continually swears and invokes the name will certainly not be cleansed from sin.
units.Sirach 23:11: A man of many oaths will be filled with lawlessness, and a scourge will not depart from his house. If he offends, his sin is upon him; if he disregards it, he has sinned twice. If he swore in vain, he will not be justified, for his house will be filled with calamities.
units.Sirach 23:12: There is an expression comparable to death; let it not be found in Jacob’s inheritance. For all these things will depart from the godly, and they will not wallow in sins.
units.Sirach 23:13: Do not accustom your mouth to crude ignorance, for sinful speech is in it.
units.Sirach 23:14: Remember your father and mother, for you sit among dignitaries, lest you forget yourself before them and become foolish through your habit; then you will wish you had not been born and curse the day of your birth.
units.Sirach 23:15: A person accustomed to words of reproach will certainly not be instructed throughout all his days.
units.Sirach 23:16: Two kinds multiply sins, and the third will bring wrath:
units.Sirach 23:17: a heated soul, like a burning fire, will certainly not be quenched until it is consumed; a sexually immoral man in his fleshly body will certainly not stop until he kindles a fire. Every loaf is sweet to a sexually immoral man; he will certainly not cease until he dies.
units.Sirach 23:18: A man who transgresses from his marriage bed says in his soul, “Who sees me? Darkness is around me, and the walls cover me; no one sees me. What should I fear? The Most High will certainly not remember my sins.”
units.Sirach 23:19: Human eyes are what he fears; he does not know that the Lord’s eyes are ten thousand times brighter than the sun, surveying every human way and observing hidden places.
units.Sirach 23:20: Before all things were created, they were known to Him, and likewise after they were completed.
units.Sirach 23:21: This man will receive retribution in the city’s squares and be seized where he did not suspect it.
units.Sirach 23:22: So also a woman who leaves her husband and presents an heir from another man.
units.Sirach 23:23: For first she disobeyed the law of the Most High; second she wronged her husband; and third she committed adultery in sexual immorality and presented children from another man.
units.Sirach 23:24: She will be brought before the assembly, and there will be a visitation upon her children.
units.Sirach 23:25: Her children will not spread out into a root, and her branches will not bear fruit.
units.Sirach 23:26: She will leave her memory as a curse, and her reproach will not be erased.
units.Sirach 23:27: Those left behind will know that nothing is better than the fear of the Lord, and nothing sweeter than attending to the Lord’s commandments.
units.Sirach 24:1: Wisdom will praise her own soul and boast in the midst of her people.
units.Sirach 24:2: She will open her mouth in the assembly of the Most High and boast before His host:
units.Sirach 24:3: “I came forth from the mouth of the Most High and covered the earth like mist.
units.Sirach 24:4: I dwelt in the heights, and my throne was in a pillar of cloud.
units.Sirach 24:5: Alone I encircled heaven’s circuit and walked in the depth of the abysses.
units.Sirach 24:6: In the waves of the sea, in all the earth, and in every people and nation I gained possession.
units.Sirach 24:7: Among all these I sought rest, and in whose inheritance I might lodge.
units.Sirach 24:8: Then the Creator of all commanded me; my Creator settled my tent and said, ‘Dwell in Jacob, and receive your inheritance in Israel.’
units.Sirach 24:9: Before the age, from the beginning, He created me, and for ever I will certainly not cease.
units.Sirach 24:10: I ministered before Him in the holy tent, and thus I was established in Zion.
units.Sirach 24:11: Likewise He settled me in the beloved city, and my authority was in Jerusalem.
units.Sirach 24:12: I took root in a glorified people, in the Lord’s portion, His inheritance.
units.Sirach 24:13: I rose high like a cedar in Lebanon, like a cypress in the mountains of Hermon.
units.Sirach 24:14: I rose high like a palm in En-gedi, like rose plants in Jericho, like a stately olive in the plain; I rose high like a plane tree.
units.Sirach 24:15: Like cinnamon and aromatic aspalathus I gave a scent; like choice myrrh I spread fragrance, like galbanum, onycha, and stacte, and like a cloud of frankincense in a tent.
units.Sirach 24:16: Like a terebinth I spread out my branches, and my branches were branches of glory and grace.
units.Sirach 24:17: Like a vine I sprouted grace, and my blossoms were fruit of glory and wealth.
units.Sirach 24:19: Come to me, you who desire me, and be filled from my produce.
units.Sirach 24:20: For my memory is sweeter than honey, and my inheritance than a honeycomb.
units.Sirach 24:21: Those who eat me will still hunger, and those who drink me will still thirst.
units.Sirach 24:22: The one who obeys me will not be ashamed, and those who work in me will not sin.”
units.Sirach 24:23: All these things are the book of the covenant of God Most High, the law which Moses commanded us as an inheritance for the assemblies of Jacob,
units.Sirach 24:25: which fills with wisdom like the Pishon, like the Tigris in the days of new crops,
units.Sirach 24:26: which fills with understanding like the Euphrates, like the Jordan in the days of harvest,
units.Sirach 24:27: which makes instruction appear like light, like the Gihon in the days of vintage.
units.Sirach 24:28: The first did not come to know her fully, and likewise the last did not trace her out.
units.Sirach 24:29: For her thought grew abundant from the sea, and her counsel from a great abyss.
units.Sirach 24:30: I too came out like a channel from a river, like a watercourse into a garden.
units.Sirach 24:31: I said, “I will water my garden and drench my garden bed.” Then behold, my channel became a river, and my river became a sea.
units.Sirach 24:32: I will again make instruction shine like the dawn and reveal these things far away.
units.Sirach 24:33: I will again pour out teaching like prophecy and leave it for generations of ages.
units.Sirach 24:34: See that I have labored not for myself alone, but for all who seek her.
units.Sirach 25:1: In three things I was adorned and stood beautiful before the Lord and human beings: harmony among brothers, friendship among neighbors, and a wife and husband living agreeably with one another.
units.Sirach 25:2: But my soul hated three kinds, and I was greatly offended at their life: a proud poor person, a rich liar, and an old adulterer deficient in understanding.
units.Sirach 25:3: You have not gathered in youth; how could you find anything in your old age?
units.Sirach 25:4: How fitting is judgment for gray hair, and knowledge of counsel for elders!
units.Sirach 25:5: How fitting is wisdom for the old, and thought and counsel for the honored!
units.Sirach 25:6: Long experience is the crown of the old, and their boast is the fear of the Lord.
units.Sirach 25:7: Nine things I considered happy in my heart, and the tenth I will speak with my tongue: a person rejoicing in children, one who lives to see his enemies’ fall;
units.Sirach 25:8: happy is the one who lives with an understanding wife, who has not slipped with his tongue, and who has not served someone unworthy of him;
units.Sirach 25:9: happy is the one who has found prudence and the one who speaks into listening ears.
units.Sirach 25:10: How great is the one who has found wisdom! Yet he is not above the one who fears the Lord.
units.Sirach 25:11: The fear of the Lord has surpassed everything; to whom will the one who holds it fast be compared?
units.Sirach 25:13: Any wound, but not a wound of the heart; any evil, but not a woman’s evil;
units.Sirach 25:14: any calamity, but not a calamity from those who hate; any retribution, but not the retribution of enemies.
units.Sirach 25:15: There is no head beyond a snake’s head, and no anger beyond an enemy’s anger.
units.Sirach 25:16: I would choose to live with a lion and a dragon rather than live with an evil woman.
units.Sirach 25:17: A woman’s evil changes her appearance and darkens her face like a bear.
units.Sirach 25:18: Her husband will recline among his neighbors and involuntarily groan bitterly.
units.Sirach 25:19: Every evil is small beside a woman’s evil; may a sinner’s lot fall upon her.
units.Sirach 25:20: A sandy ascent under an old person’s feet—so is a talkative wife to a quiet husband.
units.Sirach 25:21: Do not fall for a woman’s beauty, and do not long for a woman.
units.Sirach 25:22: Wrath, shamelessness, and great shame result if a wife supplies her husband.
units.Sirach 25:23: An evil wife is a humbled heart, a gloomy face, and a wound of the heart; one who will not make her husband happy is slack hands and paralyzed knees.
units.Sirach 25:24: From a woman came the beginning of sin, and because of her we all die.
units.Sirach 25:25: Do not give water an outlet, or an evil wife freedom of speech.
units.Sirach 25:26: If she does not walk according to your direction, cut her off from your flesh.
